trap-superlative.evidence: 'This reproduces standard spin-statistics without external postulates.' The claim is maximum-strength, unqualified — and contradicted by the proof it interprets. prf:nuclear-spin-parity's argument turns on the posited dictionary 'Knots carry half-integral spin; links carry integral spin', which is an external postulate: component count does not determine spin as a matter of topology, and nothing in the block derives it. The adverbs in the first sentence ('strictly', 'algebraically') pull the same way.
trap-superlative.notes: flagged, not fixed — the sentence's truth depends on whether the knot/link spin dictionary is derived or assumed, which is an open question in the parent proof (and is entangled with the Borromean component-count finding recorded there). Proposed: 'The SU_q(2) tensor-product rules reproduce standard spin-statistics from the knot/link spin assignment.' — which states the dependency instead of denying it.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: 'Formulating parity strictly via SU_q(2) tensor-product rules algebraically embeds empirical parity constraints within the theory.' A gerund subject carrying a prepositional phrase and an adverb, then a second adverb, before the verb finally arrives at 'embeds' — twelve words in. Read aloud the listener has lost the thread by 'algebraically'. With the block only two sentences long and the second one headed by a bare 'This', the whole block is eye-syntax.
trap-nonspeakable.notes: flagged, not fixed (same rewrite as the superlative entry resolves both). Proposed: 'The SU_q(2) tensor-product rules fix the spin parity algebraically: J is integral exactly when A is even.'
